questions.title: Which country will win the men's team gymnastics gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.background: The Commonwealth Games men's team gymnastics competition awards medals according to the final team standings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Commonwealth Games results, corroborated by contemporary reliable news reporting. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the country awarded gold in the men's team gymnastics competition at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, once the final standings are announced. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the winning country.
questions.current_reasoning: England has won three consecutive Commonwealth Games men's team gymnastics gold medals (2014, 2018, 2022), winning Birmingham 2022 by 13.35 points, and four-time Birmingham gold medallist Jake Jarman is an Official Ambassador for Glasgow 2026. Australia named a young squad with four debutants alongside Jesse Moore (top trials AA 77.550) and host Scotland named a solid but lower-difficulty team, leaving 2022 silver medallists Canada (2024 Olympic team finalists) as England's primary challenger. Accounting for modest roster uncertainty ahead of England's and Canada's final team announcements plus team-final fall variance, England is a 74% favorite.

questions.title: Which country will announce a new multinational maritime coalition to protect navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden by August 1, 2026?
questions.background: Attacks on commercial shipping since 2023 have heightened concerns about the security of maritime trade routes through the Red Sea.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country that announces the creation of a new multinational maritime coalition between July 1 and August 1, 2026, inclusive, with a stated purpose of protecting freedom of navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden. Joining an existing coalition does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No country has announced a new Red Sea/Bab al-Mandeb/Gulf of Aden multinational maritime coalition through 2026-07-15, but sharp July 13-15 regional escalation materially strengthens the case for a Saudi- or Egyptian-led initiative over a US-led one. On July 15 (Irish Times, Straits Times/Reuters), following the US's renewed Iran naval blockade and Houthi ballistic missile strikes on Saudi Arabia that broke the four-year Yemen truce, Iran's IRGC threatened to close 'all other export corridors that benefit the US and its allies'—putting Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Yanbu export bypass and Bab al-Mandeb directly in the crosshairs after Houthi officials warned of closing Bab al-Mandeb in an 'operational alliance' with Hormuz. Simultaneously, Reuters reported July 15 that commercial shipping companies are refusing US military-guided Hormuz transits after five vessel attacks since July 7—reducing the appeal and diplomatic feasibility of a brand-new US-branded coalition (especially since Operation Prosperity Guardian already exists and US forces are tied down fighting Iran). Lifting Saudi Arabia 0.20 -> 0.24 (leader of the Red Sea Council with existential Yanbu stakes) and Egypt 0.16 -> 0.17 (Suez Canal exposure, CTF 153 commander), trimming United States 0.14 -> 0.12, and holding United Kingdom (0.10) and France (0.09), leaving 28% residual for China, India, UAE, Greece, Bahrain, Turkey, Italy, or others.

local_articles.title: Iran tells Houthis to close Red Sea gateway if US hits power network, sources say
local_articles.snippet: DUBAI – Iran has asked Yemen’s Houthi movement to stand ready to close the Red Sea oil route if the United States strikes Iranian power infrastructure, three sources told Reuters on July 16, posing a potent new threat to global energy supplies. The idea has been discussed within the Islamic Republic’s leadership, and the message has been conveyed to Iran’s Houthi allies, two senior Iranian sources and a regional source familiar with the matter said, speaking on condition of anonymity. The sources said the Houthis had been informed recently of Tehran’s request, which has not been previously reported. They did not give further details on how it had been conveyed or whether it was after US President Donald Trump’s threat to attack Iranian power infrastructure on July 14. questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-10 to 2026-07-13 epidemiological updates (Reuters, AP/Al Jazeera, Economist/Hindustan Times): DRC confirmed Ebola cases jumped to 1,926 with 702 deaths (+167 cases, +102 deaths in 4 days). On July 12-13, DRC's INSP officially confirmed cases in Tshopo (4 cases, 2 deaths) and Haut-Uele (1 death) and declared both official epidemic zones, while Economist/HT revealed a confirmed Ebola victim from Ituri received a traditional burial in Kisangani (1.5M pop, Tshopo capital) with aid officials warning local urban transmission is 'a question of days.' Because an uncontained urban Bundibugyo wave in Kisangani (with no approved vaccine; Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV only entered a 50-person UK Phase 1 trial July 13) aligns tightly with a mid-September surge (~8-10 weeks out), Tshopo jumps 0.22 -> 0.30 (#2) and Haut-Uele rises 0.09 -> 0.12. Conversely, North Kivu drops sharply 0.24 -> 0.16 and South Kivu 0.04 -> 0.02 after WHO Emergencies Director Chikwe Ihekweazu told Reuters (July 10) almost all new North Kivu cases come from known contact lists and Reuters (July 13) reported AFC/M23 contained its Goma/Bukavu zones (only 4 total cases, strict border quarantines, outbreak declared over after 21 days). Ituri remains #1 (0.36 -> 0.34) amid 80% unlinked cases in Bunia, ~50% test positivity, and a July 13 pay strike halting Rwampara General Hospital (residual 6% for Kinshasa/Bas-Uele/Maniema).
